name: Boards of Canada
label: Warp
lede: Two brothers from the Pentland Hills, Michael Sandison and Marcus Eoin, make music that sounds like a home video someone taped over. In 2013 they announced an album by hiding six-digit codes in a 12-inch, a radio playlist and a cartoon ad.

eras.title: Tapes, a ruin and a hexagon
eras.text: Michael Sandison and Marcus Eoin spend a decade making tapes for family and friends. The studio name, the hexagon and the sound all exist before anyone outside the circle hears a note.

years.src: Wikipedia: Boards of Canada
years.h: Marcus Eoin joins his brother Michael Sandison's band on bass
years.p: The name comes from the National Film Board of Canada, whose documentaries the brothers watched as kids in Calgary.
years.xp:
According to Wikipedia, [[Michael Sandison|d35d0684-42bd-4344-b8a4-f18eb806801a]] (born 1971) and [[Marcus Eoin|74edfdf2-4e76-4031-ae9b-16f1c7b4ba06]] (born 1973) were born in Scotland and spent part of their childhood in Calgary, where their father worked on Saddledome construction. The NFB films they saw there became the band's name and, later, a steady supply of samples.

Both later went to the University of Edinburgh. Sandison studied English literature; Eoin studied artificial intelligence and dropped out.

years.src: Wikipedia: Boards of Canada
years.h: A cassette on Music70, the brothers' own label
years.p: Catalog number 3 on their own imprint, and the earliest release on the band's Wikipedia list.
years.xp: Wikipedia also lists a 1989 tape, Acid Memories, made when the group was Sandison, Eoin and electronics player Chris Horne. The only trace is a 24-second excerpt of one track, "Duffy", on an EHX website.

years.src: Wikipedia: Boards of Canada · Uncut: Boards Of Canada interviewed
years.h: Redmoon nights in a ruin in the Pentland Hills
years.p: Music-and-visuals gatherings in a ruined building near the brothers' studio, which Wikipedia dates to 1992 through 1994.
years.xp:
In the summer of 1995 the brothers formally named the studio Hexagon Sun, and the group began holding spring and summer gatherings under that name.

The hexagon stuck. In an Uncut interview the band said it stands for "being able to see reality for what it is, the raw maths or patterns that make everything."

years.src: Wikipedia: Twoism
years.h: About 100 copies of Twoism leave the house
years.p: Self-released, and the first record to reach anyone outside the circle. By 2001 copies were changing hands for as much as £800, according to Wikipedia.
years.xp: Recorded at Hexagon Sun with Horne contributing to production. One track, "Melissa Juice", was co-written by Horne, who asked to have his name removed when Warp reissued the EP in 2002.

eras.title: Autechre passes it along
eras.text: A copy of Twoism reaches Sean Booth of Autechre, and Booth points the duo toward a Manchester label.

years.h: Chris Horne leaves, and the brothers carry on as a duo
years.p: Wikipedia dates Horne's exit to early 1996. From here Boards of Canada is Sandison and Eoin alone.

years.src: Wikipedia: Boards of Canada · Wikipedia: Skam Records
years.h: Autechre's Sean Booth sends them to Skam
years.p: Booth got a copy of Twoism and told the brothers to send a tape to Manchester's Skam Records. The result is the Hi Scores EP.
years.xp:
Wikipedia describes Skam as a Manchester label founded around 1990 by Andy Maddocks. Its first 12-inch was a single by Lego Feet, Booth and Rob Brown before they became [[Autechre|410c9baf-5469-44f6-9852-826524b80c61]]. It prints album titles in braille on the packaging.

Sources differ on whether Booth heard Twoism or Hi Scores first. The main Boards of Canada page says Twoism.

eras.title: Two labels, one debut
eras.text: Warp and Skam release the first album jointly. A John Peel session and an EP about Waco follow.

years.cap: Stage shots from the Warp 10th anniversary party, Old Truman Brewery, London
years.src: Wikipedia: Music Has the Right to Children
years.h: Warp and Skam both release Music Has the Right to Children
years.p: Recorded 1995 to 1997 at Hexagon Sun. The cover is a family photo shot at Banff Springs, Alberta, with the faces scrubbed out.
years.xp:
Warp had been chasing the duo at the same time as Skam, so the debut came out on both. Wikipedia credits it with a 10 from Pitchfork.

AllMusic, quoted by Wikipedia, called it "a landmark for electronic listening music that was widely copied."
play: Music Has the Right to Children

years.src: Wikipedia: Peel Session (Boards of Canada EP) · Internet Archive: Boards of Canada Live - 1999-11-05
years.h: A Peel session at Maida Vale, minus the track with the sample problem
years.p: Four tracks were taped for [[John Peel|e4dec348-ad10-43b6-a2b1-c22aab890675]]'s BBC show; "XYZ" stayed off the 1999 EP because of sample licensing.
years.xp:
Warp put the session out as a three-track EP on 11 January 1999. The group swapped in a re-recorded studio version of "Happy Cycling" because the live take was judged unsatisfactory. "XYZ" finally appeared in a 2019 reissue for Warp's 30th anniversary.

The clip is a fan recording of their set at the Warp 10th anniversary party in London on 5 November 1999. The Internet Archive listing has "Happy Cycling", "Telephasic Workshop" and "In a Beautiful Place Out in the Country" on it, and notes that sources disagree on what each track is.

years.cap: Sandison and Eoin at the Incredible Warp Lighthouse Party, London, 14 October 2000
years.src: Wikipedia: In a Beautiful Place Out in the Country
years.h: In a Beautiful Place Out in the Country takes on Waco
years.p: Four tracks circle the Branch Davidians. The title is lifted from a TV interview with Amo Bishop Roden, widow of David Koresh's rival George Roden.
years.xp: Wikipedia reports a Pitchfork score of 8.9 and a spot at number 12 on the site's later list of the 50 best IDM albums. Reviewer Ben Cardew called it the point where "ecstasy succumbs to doubt."

eras.title: The dark one, then the guitar one
eras.text: Geogaddi goes darker, The Campfire Headphase picks up guitars, and Warp pulls a few stunts on the band's behalf.

years.cap: Boards of Canada at the Incredible Warp Lighthouse Party, London
q: We're too busy to give a shit.
years.src: Wikipedia: Geogaddi · Uncut: Boards Of Canada interviewed
years.h: Out of 90-plus tracks, 22 make Geogaddi
years.p: Recorded 1999 to 2001 at Hexagon Sun. Sandison says September 11 pushed them into a darker record, per Wikipedia.
years.xp:
The record leans on numerology, occult imagery and cult references, including sampled quotes about David Koresh on "1969". In the Uncut interview the band said Warp made hearing it "as difficult as possible," premiering it in six churches worldwide with turquoise hexagons where the hymn books would be.

Wikipedia lists a Japan release on 8 January 2002, ahead of the European release.

years.src: Wikipedia: Twoism
years.h: Warp reissues Twoism for everyone who couldn't find it
years.p: Horne asked for his name to come off the co-written "Melissa Juice". The reissue also trims "Sixtyniner" from 5:40 to 5:14.

years.src: Wikipedia: The Campfire Headphase
years.h: The Campfire Headphase trades synths for treated guitars
years.p: Sandison called it a "conventional band gone over the edge" (Wikipedia). Pitchfork's Mark Richardson gave it 7.6.
years.xp:
Wikipedia says the album was recorded 2003 to 2005 at Hexagon Sun. Two tracks came out ahead of it: "Oscar See Through Red Eye" on 5 September 2005 and "Dayvan Cowboy" on 4 October 2005.

Richardson found the guitars connect the music to "the pastoral tradition of British folk" but wished the "blissed-out narcotic interludes" came more often.

years.src: Wikipedia: Trans Canada Highway (EP)
years.h: The Trans Canada Highway EP comes with a skydiving video
years.p: Six tracks, 28 minutes. The "Dayvan Cowboy" video cuts skydiver Joseph Kittinger against surfer Laird Hamilton.
years.xp: Pitchfork scored the EP 6.0. Wikipedia notes the video later placed on Pitchfork's list of the top 50 music videos of the 2000s.

eras.title: A blank 12-inch and a scavenger hunt
eras.text: Warp announces Tomorrow's Harvest without announcing it: a 12-inch, a radio playlist and a puzzle fans have to solve to learn the album exists.

years.big: "There's only six of these in the world."
years.src: Vice: Boards of Canada and Music's Weirdest, Smartest Scavenger Hunt · SPIN: Boards of Canada Code Crackers
years.h: A blank 12-inch turns up at Other Music on Record Store Day
years.p: Store manager Josh Madell, on an unmarked record that runs 20 seconds: static, wobbly modular synth chords and a robot voice reading six numbers.
years.xp:
A Warp rep dropped off the records with instructions to display them without explanation. Madell: "I got this 12-inch. I honestly don't know what the details are, but there's only six of these in the world."

NYU student JR Chaparro found the copy at Other Music in New York and posted it to Reddit, suspecting some kind of marketing. Vice reports the other publicly identified copies were at Rough Trade and Avalanche Records in Edinburgh.

years.cap: Sandison and Eoin on a coastal path, press photo, c. 2013
years.src: Fresh On The Net: Tomorrow's Harvest Promotion · Vice: Boards of Canada and Music's Weirdest, Smartest Scavenger Hunt
years.h: Zane Lowe, NPR and an Adult Swim ad each hand fans six more digits
years.p: Every source carried another six-digit chunk, and the fans stitched them together.
years.xp:
Fresh On The Net's timeline: a second code turned up in a YouTube video posted under the old name Hell Interface. BBC Radio 1 aired one after a Jon Hopkins track, NPR's All Songs Considered another. SoundCloud files had to be inverted and layered, and a Base64 challenge produced the last piece.

On 27 April a projection at the Loading Bay art gallery in London showed desert footage with the Warp logo; Adult Swim broadcast the same film in the US.

years.src: Fresh On The Net: Tomorrow's Harvest Promotion · SPIN: Boards of Canada Code Crackers
years.h: Every band website now redirects to Cosecha Transmisiones
years.p: Enter the full code and it unlocks a video confirming Tomorrow's Harvest, plus a pre-order link.

years.src: Fresh On The Net: Tomorrow's Harvest Promotion
years.h: A video on Tokyo street screens, then "Reach for the Dead"
years.p: Fresh On The Net dates the Tokyo video and the single to 22 and 23 May.

years.src: Wikipedia: Tomorrow's Harvest · Fresh On The Net: Tomorrow's Harvest Promotion
years.h: The listening party is at an abandoned California waterpark
years.p: Lake Dolores Waterpark hosted it. Days earlier the band posted a distorted clip called "Look Sad Reel", an anagram of the location.

years.cap: Sandison and Eoin on a beach, press portrait, June 2013
years.src: Wikipedia: Tomorrow's Harvest
years.h: Tomorrow's Harvest earns Best New Music at Pitchfork
years.p: The first album since The Campfire Headphase in 2005. Pitchfork's Mark Richardson scored it 8.3.
years.xp:
On 3 June the band streamed the whole album on YouTube; Wikipedia says the official site crashed under "phenomenal demand." Release dates vary by source between 4 and 5 June in Japan, 10 June in Europe and 11 June in the US.

Sandison described "a deliberate VHS video-nasty element throughout the record" and said the album is about "an inevitable stage that lies in front of us," rejecting readings of it as post-apocalyptic.

eras.title: Nobody home
eras.text: Remixes, a two-hour radio mix and a 2013 website that keeps flickering. Then a hint.

years.src: Wikipedia: Boards of Canada
years.h: NTS airs a two-hour Societas X Tape mix for Warp's 30th
years.p: Wikipedia says it mixed Grace Jones, Devo and Yellow Magic Orchestra with unreleased material from the band.

years.src: Nialler9: Boards of Canada - Inferno: A timeline
years.h: The dormant 2013 website posts a message in Morse code
years.p: The words appear in English and Morse on cosecha-transmisiones.com, the site built for the Tomorrow's Harvest hunt.
years.xp: Nialler9's timeline says the site redirected to a Tomorrow's Harvest video on 29 August 2025. In between, on 15 August, the band posted a video marking 30 years since Twoism and started replying to fan comments on Instagram about new music.

eras.title: Tapes in the mail
eras.text: Warp mails VHS cassettes to customers, glues posters up in four cities and gives reviewers three plays of the album.

years.src: Nialler9: Boards of Canada - Inferno: A timeline · The Line of Best Fit: Boards of Canada reveal details
years.h: Unrequested VHS tapes with a hexagon logo arrive in the mail
years.p: Nialler9 says they carry static, an ambient soundscape and audio from a vintage Moody Bible Institute magazine ad.
years.xp: Wikipedia says the tapes went to Warp customers' home addresses. On 15 April, Warp posted street posters of zombified children with the Hexagon Sun logo; The Line of Best Fit reports posters in London, Tokyo, Los Angeles and New York.

years.cap: Sandison and Eoin in a promo photo for the Inferno announcement, c. 2026
years.src: Nialler9: Boards of Canada - Inferno: A timeline · Stereogum: Boards Of Canada Share New Singles
years.h: "Tape 05" is 3:21 of ambient music with a harp melody
years.p: The first new music in 13 years ends up on Inferno as "Deep Time". The album is announced six days later.
years.xp: Nialler9 dates the announcement to 22 April: fifth album, 18 tracks, out 29 May on Warp, with a 42-second trailer built around a hexagon. Seven listening sessions were set for 22 May, with record shops hosting parties on 28 May.

years.src: Stereogum: Boards Of Canada Share New Singles
years.h: "Introit" and "Prophecy at 1420 MHz" open the album
years.p: Stereogum describes "Introit" as a 36-second intro and the second track as a midtempo groove with computerized narration. Robert Beatty directed the video.

years.src: Wikipedia: Inferno (Boards of Canada album)
years.h: The White House posts a video set to "Deep Time"
years.p: Warp said neither the label nor the duo condoned the unauthorised use of their music for political messaging, per Wikipedia.

years.src: Wikipedia: Inferno (Boards of Canada album)
years.h: Inferno peaks at number 3 in the UK
years.p: Fifth album, recorded at Hexagon Sun and mastered by Matt Colton. Pitchfork's Philip Sherburne scored it 8.6.
years.xp:
Wikipedia reports 69:51 of music, 21 Metacritic reviews averaging 85, and streams limited to three plays for reviewers. Rolling Stone called the rollout a "noisy anti-campaign."

It peaked at number 3 on the UK Albums Chart and number 29 on the Billboard 200. Clash and Uncut both gave it 9 out of 10, and Wikipedia summarizes Pitchfork's review as reading it as an investigation of faith, human biology and existential doubt.
